title: Plant-based ingredient analytical and characterization service
value_chain_segment: Raw Materials, Ingredients, & Inputs; Compliance; End Products; Investment; Production; R&D
scope_note: Ingredient testing for human-food protein
vietnam_angle: Real. Buyers already specify function (gel strength, emulsion and retort stability for meat pastes; solubility, viscosity and UHT stability for plant milks), and no Vietnamese laboratory offers functional testing as a service
vietnam_evidence: No entry in pilot_labs.csv lists functional or texture testing; one search found a dealer selling texture analysers but no fee-for-service offer (SLP-17). Buyer specifications are revealed in ch16 (BUY-05; BUY-16). Labs that could host: HUST protein characterisation group (PL-027), FIRI NACEFA (PL-002), Can Tho University Institute of Food and Biotechnology and Nguyen Tat Thanh University's hi-tech centre at Saigon Hi-Tech Park (SLP-01)
verdict_note: Extend P4 from protein quality to protein function: a standard functional panel (solubility, water and oil holding, emulsifying, foaming, gelling, per Embrapa 2022) plus buyer tests (gel strength in a sausage model, UHT stability), and an open dataset for local crops and side streams linked to the P5 atlas. Same owners and buyers as P4, so an extension, not a new public good
signal_to_watch: A Vietnamese laboratory adding functional properties to its accredited scope; a buyer (Vinamilk, Vissan) publishing an ingredient specification
source_ids: GSD-01; SLP-01; SLP-10; SLP-17; BUY-05; BUY-16

title: Biological processing methods for isolating protein ingredients
value_chain_segment: Raw Materials, Ingredients, & Inputs; End Products; Production; R&D
scope_note: Processing of plant protein for food
vietnam_angle: Mixed. Enzyme-assisted extraction from broken rice has been done in Vietnam at lab scale, and broken rice now costs less per tonne than cassava starch. But rice protein pays only as a co-product of a starch or syrup line, and we found no such host in Vietnam. The mung bean starch-water route exists in China and Thailand, not at scale in Vietnam
vietnam_evidence: Viscozyme extraction of VD20 broken rice gave about 77% protein and about 55% recovery after 36 h (SLP-01). At USD 327 to 372 per t (FS-26) and 7.9 g protein per 100 g (DIE-12), raw material alone costs USD 5.1 to 6.6 per kg of product, against USD 2 to 3 for Chinese pea protein (our calculation; TPP-05). Rice protein is a by-product of rice syrup (SLP-08). Three searches found no Vietnamese rice starch, rice syrup or rice protein maker. Broken rice USD 368 to 372 per t (FS-26) against cassava native starch USD 520 to 540 per t FOB in April 2026 (FS-11)
verdict_note: Adds a constraint to T10 (rice arm): a rice protein ingredient needs a host that sells the carbohydrate, so the rice arm is a co-product of a broken-rice saccharification line, not a stand-alone isolate plant. Adds a note to T4: broken rice is a second, protein-bearing sugar feedstock while cassava starch prices stay high. Enzymes are a tool inside T10, not a separate play
signal_to_watch: A Vietnamese starch, syrup or beer-adjunct processor announcing broken-rice saccharification; Chinese or Thai rice-protein offers to Vietnamese dairy buyers; cassava starch falling back below about USD 420 per t

title: Pooled procurement/group purchasing for ingredients and inputs
value_chain_segment: Raw Materials, Ingredients, & Inputs; Business Services
scope_note: Joint buying of soy flour or textured protein by food makers
vietnam_angle: moderate
vietnam_evidence: Law on Competition 2018 bans outright agreements fixing prices of goods among firms in the same relevant market (Art. 11(1), 12(1)); exemption possible (Art. 14). Law on Cooperatives 2023 lets 5 or more members, including Vietnamese legal persons, form a cooperative that serves members through internal transactions, with tax relief and preferential credit (Art. 4, 22, 23, 30). No chay makers' association or joint-buying group found; FFA-HCMC became a business association in November 2025 with no joint buying described.
verdict_note: T1 and section 26.7: adds a constraint and a vehicle. Pooled buying or pooled offtake should be parallel bilateral contracts with the line owner, or a cooperative of 5 or more members; an agreement among competing chay makers on the price they pay carries legal risk (our reading, not legal advice).
signal_to_watch: A chay makers' cooperative or association that buys soy flour or textured protein jointly

scope_note: Research capacity for human-food protein
maps_to: T5; P4; RM-04; RM-05; RM-09; ch06-knowledge-talent 6.4
vietnam_angle: Weak for a dedicated centre. Output is scattered: IUH, Nong Lam, HCMUT, HUST and others each have 2 to 6 records; GFI lists no Vietnamese research centre. title: Building alternative protein programs and majors at universities
scope_note: Workforce for human-food protein
vietnam_angle: Moderate. Food technology and bioengineering degrees are large (Can Tho University 300 and 240 places in 2026; HUST food engineering 360, snippet only). No alternative-protein major exists. MOET asks universities to build postgraduate biotechnology programmes on a 'CNSH+X' model (biotechnology plus an application field), with requested state lab investment
vietnam_evidence: INF-15 (Can Tho quotas); SLW-19 (HUST quotas, snippet, Low); SLW-08 (MOET Official Letter 5695, 17 September 2025); VCO-21 (0 courses)
verdict_note: Adds a named vehicle to RM-09: a 'biotechnology plus food process engineering' talent master's under Decision 1002, proposed through MOET's annual cycle. A full alternative-protein major is not justified: the job base is small (a wave 3 estimate puts a 10,000 t a year plant at 60 to 100 staff, Low)
signal_to_watch: A university proposes or is approved for a CNSH plus food or bioprocess talent programme; MOET's list of approved talent programmes

title: Increasing the number, quality, and diversity of alternative protein-relevant university courses
scope_note: Workforce and research skills
vietnam_angle: Moderate. The skills gap is specialist: extrusion, downstream processing of microbial biomass, sensory and structure of meat analogues, protein-quality scoring and food cell culture. IUH is the only Vietnamese university with recent meat-analogue papers (two in 2026). EU projects have reformed Vietnamese food curricula before (AsiFood; NutriSEA at Hue and HUST, 2015 to 2018)
vietnam_evidence: ch06 6.5 (RD-01; BIB-01); TIC-21 and SLW-18 (IUH 2026 papers); SLW-13 (NutriSEA); RD-56 (AsiFood); VCO-21 (0 courses)
verdict_note: Adds module content and a delivery route to RM-09: short specialist modules at two or three universities (IUH for texturisation, HUST for side-stream protein and fermentation, Can Tho for food technology), reusing open course material and the EU curriculum-reform model. Vietnam would adapt material, not write it from scratch
signal_to_watch: A Vietnamese-language module on extrusion or downstream processing; an Erasmus+ or similar project on food protein with Vietnamese partners
source_ids: GSD-01; TIC-21; SLW-18; SLW-13; RD-56; VCO-21

title: Fiber spinning innovations for improved plant protein texturization
value_chain_segment: R&D; End Products; Production; Raw Materials, Ingredients, & Inputs
scope_note: Texturisation of plant protein for food
vietnam_angle: None now. Vietnam has no documented texturisation capacity beyond machine dealers; the frontier is in Europe, and Thailand is far ahead in research
vietnam_evidence: Vietnam-affiliated works 2015 to 2026 on extrusion, high-moisture or shear-cell texturisation of meat analogues: 3; Thailand: 31, including high-moisture extrusion of mung bean protein (SLP-06; SLP-07). The 2026 IUH paper (TIC-21) is all-IUH by affiliation but its equipment is unverified (abstract withheld; SLP-07). No Vietnam-affiliated shear-cell or fibre-spinning work. Shear cell is commercial at 'several hundred tons a year' in the Netherlands (SLP-12)
verdict_note: Does not change T1: T1 is dry textured protein by standard extrusion, where cost is set by soy flour, not by texturising technology. Fibre spinning is still research; shear cell is an early commercial European route. Vietnam would buy equipment or licence later. For trials, Thai public extrusion capacity (MTEC, Kasetsart) is nearer than any Vietnamese facility
signal_to_watch: A shear-cell or spinning unit sold or licensed in Asia; a published cost per kg below high-moisture extrusion; confirmation that IUH holds a food extruder (OQ-386)
source_ids: GSD-01; SLP-06; SLP-07; SLP-12; TIC-21; FORM-34

title: From dependency to diversity: a strategic scenario analysis on reducing Europe's soy import dependency by 2035
scope_note: Method in scope; its feed and diet-change levers are context or out of scope for Vietnam
maps_to: RM-01; RM-13; ch22 sections 22.2 and 22.5; app-f4; PSB-009; OQ-462
vietnam_angle: Vietnam imports 98.4% of its soybeans and about 99% of the soy protein it feeds. The study already has the same data foundation (FAO food balance sheets, protein by origin and use) and a forward balance model; what transfers is the target-first back-calculation with feasibility grading and a domestic-feed-only stress test
vietnam_evidence: Run on the study's own numbers (our calculation, tools/vn_backcalc.py): imported soy protein 3.50 Mt in 2025 (feed 3.31, food 0.19); a 20% cut below 2025 by 2035 needs 1.74 Mt of protein (3.8 Mt soybean-meal equivalent) against the S-BASE trend, because trend demand grows 30%. In-scope levers deliver about 9% to 11% of that (domestic soybean at the 2010 area 7.6% to 9.7%, or 14.6% at the 300 kha proposal; D-STRETCH food routes 1.1%); feed efficiency (S-EFF, outside scope) 36.6%; S-ALT 12.1%
verdict_note: The method runs for Vietnam with data the study already holds, except the side-stream and farm-economics levers. It confirms ch22: imports cannot be held near the 2025 level by in-scope levers, and the one in-scope lever with weight for the protein people eat directly is domestic food soybean. Present a feasibility-graded table in app-f4; no change to RM-01 beyond that
signal_to_watch: EU Comprehensive Protein Plan follow-up and the EU harmonised protein balance sheet (VIS-15); China's soy import reduction objective

title: Towards a Legume Renaissance in Europe: a practical roadmap for fava beans for food and feed
scope_note: Food legumes in scope; the feed half is context only
maps_to: T10; T1; P6; OQ-463; OQ-094; PSB-006; PSB-010; ch22 section 22.3
vietnam_angle: The roadmap method (one crop, a value-chain taskforce with buyers, a barrier map, a farm-archetype economics model, then policy asks tied to named instruments) fits Vietnam's food soybean, not its feed soybean. Soy foods carry about 181,000 t of protein a year on 97.5% imported beans; domestic non-GM beans have a named buyer with a breeding programme
vietnam_evidence: Food soybean use 540 kt (2025); domestic output 42 to 43 kt; area 205 kha in 2010; domestic beans 25,000 to 30,000 VND/kg against 13,000 to 15,000 for imports (2024), or 1.4 to 1.7 times the 2023 Canadian import unit value of USD 686/t (our calculation); Vinasoy's VSAC holds 2,072 soybean lines and VINASOY 05 yields above 2.5 t/ha at Cu Jut, and QNS plans to invest in soybean raw-material areas in 2026; 654 kha of rice land planned for release by 2030; crop strategy has no soybean target; we found no Vietnamese farm-economics study of soybean or mung bean in rotations
verdict_note: PPE-C1: domestic food-grade soybean (and mung bean) for soy foods and plant drinks, with a buyer-led value-chain taskforce and a farm-economics test as step one. Beats T1 and T10 on public value (domestic inputs for protein people already eat); weak on Vietnam advantage (cost) and defensibility
signal_to_watch: Tonnage of domestic beans bought by Vinasoy and tofu makers (OQ-463); farm-gate soybean price against imported non-GM beans; whether MAE names soybean in its domestic raw-material area task

owner: Alt: Meat Lab and SCET, UC Berkeley
scope_note: Teaching and venture building for protein for people
vietnam_angle: Yes. Product-development skills tied to buyer problems is a gap that no study public good covers (P1, P4, P5, P6 are rules, a laboratory and data; RM-09 is process engineering). T1 and T10 need buyer specifications and functional trials before a plant. A national platform for student food innovation already exists.
vietnam_evidence: HUIT's Food Innovation and Development (FID) contest 2025: nearly 500 contestants, 144 projects from 58 universities and high schools, a firm-judged table with 10 enterprise prizes, co-organised by VAFoST and the National Startup Support Center; no plant-protein product among the 2025 winners (AML-33). A 2023 season had a plant-based theme (snippet only, AML-34). ch06 records almost no Vietnamese work on sensory and structure of meat analogues. We found no credit-bearing Vietnamese course with alternative-protein content (one search; L6 owns the inventory).
verdict_note: Proposed as AML-C1 (buyer-set protein product challenge lab), balanced score 2.95 (our calculation). Berkeley ran the format from Spring 2017 to Spring 2024: 4-unit classes, entry by application, simulated startup teams on industry-set problems, about 32 students a semester, at least three startups. Merge with any L6 proposal under GFI-023 or GFI-024.
signal_to_watch: A Vietnamese chay maker, plant-milk maker or fermenter sets and pays for a student problem at FID or at a food-technology faculty; L6 course inventory
